answer: A farm running 38 keys therefore burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the kernel stake is held until the juniper settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the quartz audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 18% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. That is 5 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
